# FFmpeg glitch, glow, CRT and halftone effects for real footage

**A clip you own gets glow, glitch, CRT, chromatic aberration, halftone, zoom blur or heat haze from tested FFmpeg chains.**

<p><img src="https://s3.varg.ai/files/194b94d0-58ff-4e8b-91de-4f1959d04013/file_69a257232639.webp" alt="Film footage cycles through four looks: warm halation glow on rooftops, a curved CRT screen, an RGB-split digital glitch and a black-and-white halftone." width="480"><br><sub>Footage: Tears of Steel (CC BY 3.0) © Blender Foundation, mango.blender.org</sub></p>

Eight effects for footage you already have, each as tested ffmpeg filter chains plus HyperFrames and Remotion equivalents: glow and bloom (soft, film halation, sci-fi, sunset, anamorphic streaks, ominous), digital glitch (subtle to corrupt), CRT screen (consumer TV, arcade grille, green and amber terminal), chromatic aberration (lens, radial, linear split), halftone (ink on paper, CMY screen, LED wall, mosaic), acid photocopy, radial zoom blur and wave or heat distortion. Presets give thresholds, blur scales, offsets in px at 1080p, screen angles, ink colors, scanline periods and where in the edit each effect belongs, from Xor (GM Shaders), the libretro CRT shaders, GPU Gems, Steve Yedlin and Andrew Kramer. Use when someone wants a glitch, glow, VHS-era CRT, halftone, chromatic or heat-haze look on a clip, or a zoom-blur punch on the beat. NOT for color grading and LUTs, animated backgrounds without footage (paper-shaders) or generating new footage (varg-ai).

```bash
npx skills add vargHQ/skills --skill footage-effects                # Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Gemini CLI, OpenCode…
gh skill install vargHQ/skills footage-effects --agent github-copilot --scope user
# or all 73 skills as a Claude Code plugin:
claude plugin marketplace add vargHQ/skills
claude plugin install varg@varg
```

- "Add short glitch bursts on the cuts of ./clip.mp4 with ffmpeg"
- "Put ./interview.mp4 on a green phosphor CRT screen"
- "Make ./skate.mp4 look like a halftone print on paper"
